title: Length of longest increasing subsequence
statement_markdown:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from an array by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101], therefore the length is 4.

hints: A standard dynamic programming approach (O(n^2)) works well here.
Let `dp[i]` be the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends with `nums[i]`.
explanation: We can solve this with dynamic programming. We create an array `dp` of the same length as `nums`, initialized to 1. Then we iterate through `nums` with an outer loop `i`. Inside, an inner loop `j` from 0 to `i-1` checks if `nums[i] > nums[j]`. If so, we can extend the LIS ending at `j`, updating `dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1)`. The result is the maximum value in `dp`.
